title: Part of the LMC H II region N214
caption: Part of the H II region N214 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by ESO's New Technology Telescope
celestial: N214C · constellation Mensa · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A large nebula fills the lower part of this picture, a star cluster sits from the upper left to the middle, and a string of compact reddish nebulae lies at the top right. Together they are part of N214, a region of glowing gas in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small galaxy near our own.

Regions like this are called H II regions. Hot young stars pour out energetic light that strips hydrogen atoms of their electrons, and the gas glows as a result. The big nebula at the bottom is known as N214C.

The reddish knots at the upper right are N214H. The new observations show that it is made of four compact H II regions, each with its own star lighting it up, plus a more diffuse nebula. The image was made by combining many exposures taken through a mix of narrow and broad filters, which pick out light from particular gases as well as overall color.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.91 x 5.22 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 193 × 258 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This six-color composite was taken with the SuSI2 camera on ESO's New Technology Telescope in visible light, using narrowband filters such as hydrogen-alpha, hydrogen-beta and oxygen alongside broadband ones. The color mapping isn't published.
filters: 486 nm · Optical H-beta (New Technology Telescope SUSI2)

understand.eye: Narrowband filters isolate the light of individual gases, and co-added exposures build up detail that an eye could not see.

explore: The field of view is 248 by 332 arcseconds, which corresponds to roughly 200 by 270 light-years. North is up and east is to the left. The region is about 170,000 light-years from Earth.
alt: A large nebula at the bottom, a star cluster from upper left to center, and a group of compact reddish nebulae at top right.
